record.paper_title: Open Questions Related to Bose-Einstein Correlations in e+e− → Hadrons
record.original_question: Does the observed hadron-mass dependence of the emitter dimension r(m), measured in electron-positron annihilation and decreasing with hadron mass, also occur in particle reactions other than electron-positron annihilation?

evidence.quote: The emitter dimension r(m) is seen to decrease with the hadron mass, from ∼0.75 fm at mπ to ∼0.15 fm at mΛ.
The r(m) behaviour should be investigated also in other than e+e− particles reactions

artifact.self_contained_problem:
In the study of Bose–Einstein correlations between pairs of identical bosons produced in high-energy particle collisions, one parametrizes the two-particle correlation function

C(Q) = 1 + λ exp(−r² Q²),

where Q² = −(p₁ − p₂)² is the squared four-momentum difference of the pair, λ is the chaoticity (incoherence) parameter, and r is interpreted as the spatial extent of the emitting source for that hadron species. In e⁺e⁻ → hadrons measurements, the fitted source radius r(m), viewed as a function of the mass m of the identical-boson species used in the correlation analysis (e.g., π, K, p, Λ), is observed to decrease monotonically with m, from roughly 0.75 fm for pions down to roughly 0.15 fm for Λ baryons.

Question: Does the same qualitative and quantitative hadron-mass dependence r(m) — a monotonic decrease of the extracted Bose–Einstein (or Fermi–Dirac, in the Λ case) source radius with the mass of the identical particle species — occur in particle reactions other than e⁺e⁻ annihilation, such as hadron–hadron (e.g., pp, pp̄), lepton–hadron (e.g., ep), or heavy-ion collisions?
artifact.status_search_result: Subsequent experiments in hadronic and heavy-ion environments (e.g., LHCb pp and pPb, ATLAS pp at 13 TeV, ALICE heavy-ion measurements) have measured Bose–Einstein source radii for several hadron species, and a decrease of the extracted radius with hadron mass has been observed, consistent with the e⁺e⁻ pattern. However, a complete species-by-species mapping of r(m) across all reaction types (matching the π–K–p–Λ scan done in e⁺e⁻) has not been carried out uniformly, so the question is only partially answered.

status_evidence.title: Bose–Einstein Correlations in pp and pPb Collisions at LHCb
status_evidence.snippet: Measurements of BEC source radii in pp and pPb collisions at LHCb.
status_evidence.claim: Mass/species dependence of BEC source radii has been studied beyond e+e- reactions.

status_evidence.title: Two-particle Bose–Einstein correlations in pp collisions at √s=13 TeV with ATLAS
status_evidence.snippet: BEC parameters characterizing the source radius and correlation strength studied in pp collisions.
status_evidence.claim: BEC source radii have been measured in pp collisions, extending studies beyond e+e-.
